extracted.intended_audience: creators and users of Creative Commons-licensed works (authors, remixers, educators, publishers, and anyone reusing CC BY-SA 3.0 content)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of permissions and obligations when using, adapting, or redistributing material under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported license. Covers what is allowed, required attribution, share-alike obligations, and limitations/notice provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share (permission to copy and redistribute)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share — copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format for any purpose, even commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deed explicitly allows copying and redistribution in any medium or format and for any purpose, including commercial use. These freedoms are granted provided license terms are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt (permission to remix, transform, build upon)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt — remix, transform, and build upon the material for any purpose, even commercially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are permitted to create derivatives and adaptations and to use them commercially, subject to the license's terms (notably attribution and share-alike requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution (must give appropriate credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribution — You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the license, and indicate if changes were made. You may do so in any reasonable manner, but not in any way that suggests the licensor endorses you or your use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote guidance (original wording): 'If supplied, you must provide the name of the creator and attribution parties, a copyright notice, a license notice, a disclaimer notice, and a link to the material. CC licenses prior to Version 4.0 also require you to provide the title of the material if supplied, and may have other slight differences.' In practice include creator name, attribution parties, link to license, and note of changes; do not imply endorsement by the licensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: ShareAlike (derivatives must use same license)
rubrics_metrics.description: ShareAlike — If you remix, transform, or build upon the material, you must distribute your contributions under the same license as the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivatives must be released under CC BY-SA 3.0 (or a license listed as compatible). See https://creativecommons.org/compatiblelicenses for compatible-license options. This preserves the share-alike chain for downstream users.

rubrics_metrics.name: No additional restrictions (no legal or technological barriers)
rubrics_metrics.description: No additional restrictions — You may not apply legal terms or technological measures that legally restrict others from doing anything the license permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The license prohibits imposing effective technological measures or contract terms that would prevent others from exercising the licensed rights. 'Technological measures' are referenced to Article 11 of the WIPO Copyright Treaty; do not use DRM or similar to block permitted uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: License non-revocability (rights persist while terms followed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensor cannot revoke these freedoms as long as you follow the license terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once granted, the permissions remain in force for downstream users provided they comply with the license obligations (e.g., attribution, share-alike).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and public-domain elements (not subject to license obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not have to comply with the license for elements of the material in the public domain or where your use is permitted by an applicable exception or limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User rights under exceptions and limitations (such as fair use or fair dealing) are not affected by CC licenses. If a portion of the work is public domain or your jurisdiction allows a particular use, the license obligations may not apply to that portion or use.

rubrics_metrics.name: No warranties and other rights (additional permissions may be required)
rubrics_metrics.description: No warranties are given. The license may not give you all of the permissions necessary for your intended use. For example, other rights such as publicity, privacy, or moral rights may limit how you use the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The license disclaims warranties and notes that separate permissions (e.g., for use of someone's likeness, privacy rights, or moral rights) may still be required even if the license permits copying/adaptation. Check and obtain additional permissions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating changes (version differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if changes were made — In 4.0, you must indicate if you modified the material and retain an indication of previous modifications. In 3.0 and earlier license versions, the indication of changes is only required if you create a derivative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adapting material, follow the version-specific requirements for marking modifications. For BY-SA 3.0 specifically, you are required to indicate changes if you publish a derivative; the 4.0 rules are stricter about indicating modifications and their history.
